problem: Object-goal navigation agents search blindly and waste time. Prior ask-for-help work rarely studies agents that must stay robust when the teacher is sometimes absent at test time.
motivation: A real robot assistant can ask a nearby person where the target object is, but that person will not always be available. An agent trained only with a fully present teacher may become dependent on feedback and fail without it.
key_idea: Train an ObjectNav agent with an extra 'ask' action that returns a binary segmentation mask of the target in its view, using a curriculum that mixes episodes with and without a teacher (semi-present teacher).
insight: The agent trained with a 100% present teacher collapses without feedback (about 95% failure). Mixing in teacher-free episodes (25% or 75% teacher presence) restores no-teacher performance to roughly baseline level or better while keeping the gain when feedback is available. For example, Semi-75 reaches 72.1 SR on seen objects with the teacher and 18.5 SR on unseen objects without it. The evidence is a small single table, with no seeds or variance reported.
method: Ask action: a seventh action added to the six basic navigation actions; the agent can request help at any step.
Object-in-view feedback: on each ask, the agent receives a binary mask (1 at the target's pixels, 0 elsewhere) built from ground-truth semantic segmentation of the current view.
Semi-present teacher curriculum: the teacher, and hence the extra observation and feedback, is present in η% of training episodes (η = 25 or 75); 100% is the Feedback model.
Task setup: AI2-THOR ObjectNav with a randomly chosen target object, randomized object placement each episode, RGB-D sensor, and success when stopping within 1.0 m.
Training: PPO reinforcement learning with the Adam optimizer; evaluated with SR and SPL on seen and unseen objects.

setting.privileged: Ground-truth semantic segmentation of the target is given as feedback when the agent asks (part of the method's teacher, not a test-time cheat).

numbers_note: The split name is not stated in the paper; 'val' is used as a placeholder. Metrics are given separately for seen and unseen objects, so they are encoded as _seen/_unseen suffixes. The Baseline (no ask) row is 35.2/13.0 SR and 24.1/6.9 SPL; it is not a variant of the paper's method, so it is omitted here.
results: With the teacher present, the object-in-view feedback agent reaches 70.9 SR / 46.4 SPL on seen objects versus 35.2 / 24.1 for the baseline, an average improvement of 29.9% SR and 19.8% SPL. Semi-present curricula stay near or above the baseline when feedback is absent, for example Semi-75 gets 18.5 SR on unseen objects versus 13.0 for the baseline.
limitations: Feedback is idealized: it comes from ground-truth segmentation and takes only one form, a mask of the object in view.
The paper gives no detail on the model architecture, ask penalties, number of runs, or variance, and only a small table on one simulator.
There is no uncertainty estimate for deciding when to ask, and results are mixed: Semi-25 with a present teacher does worse than the full-feedback model.
